parts.latex:
Oscar bought 1200 shares for \$5.80 per share. He received a dividend of $6.4\%$ on his purchase price. Oscar sold these shares for \$7.50 each after three months.

Calculate his profit from the dividend and the sale of his shares.

solutions.latex:
The dividend is $6.4\%$ of the purchase price.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Dividend}&=6.4\%\times\$5.80\times1200\\ &=\$445.44\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Profit}&=1200\times7.50+445.44-1200\times5.80\\ &=9000+445.44-6960\\ &=\$2485.44\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates dividend correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Dividend yield is dividend divided by share price.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{A: }&\dfrac{0.504}{4.20}=12\%\\ \text{B: }&\dfrac{0.63}{4.50}=14\%\\ \text{C: }&\dfrac{0.608}{3.80}=16\%\\ \text{D: }&\dfrac{0.7}{3.90}\approx17.9\%\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Company D has the highest dividend yield}$$

parts.latex:
You own 400 shares in GRQ Pty Ltd.

The current share price is \$25.12 and your annual dividend income is \$282.

What is the dividend yield on your shares?

solutions.latex:
The dividend per share is
$$\dfrac{282}{400} = \$0.705$$
The dividend yield is
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{0.705}{25.12} \times 100\% &= 2.8065\ldots\% \\ &\approx 2.81\% \end{aligned}$$

7821.stem: Cameron purchased 3 500 shares in a start up company for \$4.20 each. The brokerage fee charged on purchase was 3.7 cents per share. Later that year the start up company paid a dividend of 25 cents per share. Cameron then sold the shares for \$5.25 each.

parts.latex: What was the total cost of the shares when Cameron bought them?
Calculate the dividend yield when the shares were sold. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

solutions.latex:
The cost per share is the price plus brokerage: $\$4.20+\$0.037=\$4.237$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total cost}&=3500\times 4.237\\ &=\$14\,829.50 \end{aligned}$$

meta.generated_note: Brokerage 3.7 cents = \$0.037 per share, added to purchase cost.

solutions.latex:
Dividend yield is the dividend per share divided by the share price, here the selling price of \$5.25.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Dividend yield}&=\dfrac{0.25}{5.25}\times 100\%\\ &\approx 4.76\% \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the dividend yield formula, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Question says 'when the shares were sold', so the selling price \$5.25 is used as the share price.

parts.latex: A share is valued at \$46.89. Jake buys $5100$ shares and at the end of the financial year, he receives a dividend of \$4212. The dividend yield on Jake's investment is:

solutions.latex:
The dividend yield is the dividend per share divided by the share price, as a percentage.

The dividend per share is
$$\dfrac{4212}{5100}\approx \$0.8259$$
So the yield is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Yield} &= \dfrac{0.8259}{46.89}\times 100\% \\ &\approx 1.76\% \end{aligned}$$
This is option D.
